UCLA RESEARCHERS FOUND CREATINE BEING USED
SOMEWHERE THEY DIDN'T EXPECT:
HOW CREATINE FUELS THE IMMUNE CELLS THAT
FIGHT CANCER, NOT JUST BUILD MUSCLE..

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
CREATINE MAY DO FAR MORE
THAN BUILD MUSCLE.
UCLA researchers discovered something
unexpected:
Immune cells involved in fighting tumors appear
to use creatine for energy.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
THE NEW DISCOVERY
CREATINE + CANCER IMMUNITY?
In 2026, UCLA researchers reported that
dendritic cells inside tumors increased their
machinery for taking up creatine.
Why would an immune cell need creatine?
ENERGY.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
MEET THE DENDRITIC CELL
THE IMMUNE SYSTEM'S "SCOUT."
Dendritic cells help recognize tumor-
associated material and present it to T cells.
In simple terms:
They help show killer T cells
what they should attack.
Without effective dendritic-cell activation, the
anti-tumor immune response can weaken.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
BUT THERE'S A PROBLEM
TUMORS CAN BE
ENERGY-STARVED ENVIRONMENTS.
Immune cells operating inside tumors must
compete for nutrients while carrying out
extremely energy-demanding functions.
Researchers wondered:
Could creatine help these immune cells
maintain their energy supply?

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
THINK OF CREATINE
AS AN ENERGY BUFFER
Creatine participates in the phosphocreatine
energy system, helping cells rapidly regenerate
ATP.
ATP is the cellular energy currency needed for:
activation
signaling
movement
protein synthesis
immune function
And dendritic cells appear to use this system
too.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
THE EXPERIMENT
Researchers genetically removed the creatine
transporter from dendritic cells.
The result?
The cells showed:
• survival
L activation
• ability to stimulate tumor-targeting CD8+ T
cells
Creatine uptake appeared to matter to their
function.

Holisticentral 6
@holisticentral
THEN THEY DID THE OPPOSITE
Researchers increased creatine availability.
Creatine helped dendritic cells maintain higher
intracellular ATP and supported energy-
dependent inflammatory signaling involved in
their activation.
In other words:
Creatine appeared to help keep the immune-
cell battery charged.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
THEN CAME THE TUMOR EXPERIMENT
In mouse models of melanoma, creatine
treatment:
slowed tumor growth
AND increased the abundance and activation of
tumor-infiltrating dendritic cells.
That is an intriguing finding.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
WHAT ABOUT HUMAN CELLS?
Researchers also treated human monocyte-
derived dendritic cells in the laboratory.
Creatine enhanced their activation and improved
their ability to stimulate human T cells against a
cancer-associated target.
This raises an intriguing possibility for future
cancer immunotherapy research.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
AND THIS ISN'T THE FIRST CLUE
A previous UCLA study found that CD8+ killer T
cells also depend on creatine metabolism to
support their anti-tumor activity.
So creatine may influence more than one
component of the immune response:
Dendritic cells → activate T cells
Killer T cells → attack tumor cells

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
A BIGGER IDEA EMERGES
We usually think of immunity in terms of:
antibodies
cytokines
white blood cells
inflammation
But researchers are increasingly asking another
question:
DO IMMUNE CELLS HAVE ENOUGH ENERGY
TO DO THEIR JOB?
This is the emerging world of
immunometabolism.

Holisticentral i
@holisticentral
THIS CHANGES HOW WE SEE CREATINE
For decades, creatine was largely associated
with:
muscle
strength
athletic performance
Research has increasingly explored its roles in
other energy-demanding tissues.
And now another frontier is emerging:
IMMUNE-CELL BIOENERGETICS.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
THE QUESTION
Perhaps the most interesting lesson isn't:
"Does creatine fight cancer?"
We don't know that.
The more fascinating question may be:
How much does cellular energy determine
whether the immune system can mount an
effective response?

IT SUPPORTS THE LUNGS.
IT HELPS PROTECT THE LIVER.
AND HOSPITALS USE IT AS AN EMERGENCY
MEDICINE: THE MOLECULE THAT HELPS REBUILD
YOUR BODY'S MASTER ANTIOXIDANT...

Holisticentral O
@holisticentral
NAC: THE ANTIOXIDANT BUILDER
NAC stands for:
N-Acetylcysteine
It is a stable form of cysteine—an amino
acid the body needs to manufacture one of
its most important protective molecules:
Glutathione.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
THE GLUTATHIONE CONNECTION
Glutathione helps cells:
• Neutralize reactive molecules
• Maintain antioxidant balance
• Protect proteins and cell
membranes
• Process certain compounds in
the liver
• Recover from oxidative stress
NAC supplies cysteine—often the
limiting building block in
glutathione production.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
YOUR BODY STILL DOES THE WORK
NAC is often described as a
"glutathione supplement."
But more accurately:
NAC gives the body raw material.
The body must still combine cysteine
with glycine and glutamate to
manufacture glutathione.
This is nutritional support, not a
substitute for the body's intelligence.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
WHY HOSPITALS USE IT
NAC is an established medical
treatment for acetaminophen
poisoning.
An overdose can rapidly deplete liver
glutathione and produce a toxic
metabolite that damages liver cells.
Given promptly, medical NAC helps
restore protective capacity and can
dramatically reduce liver injury.
Suspected overdose is an emergency
—not a home supplement protocol.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
IT ALSO CHANGES MUCUS
NAC is a mucolytic.
It can break chemical bonds that help
make mucus thick and sticky, allowing
secretions to become thinner and easier to
clear.
This is why acetylcysteine has long been
used medically in respiratory care.

Holisticentral C
@holisticentral
LUNGS + OXIDATIVE STRESS
NAC has been studied in conditions
involving mucus and oxidative stress,
including:
• Chronic bronchitis
• COPD
• Certain respiratory infections
• Environmental and inflammatory
stressors
Some studies report benefit in selected
patients, but outcomes vary by condition,
dose and treatment duration.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
NAC supports specific protective pathways
by:
• Replenishing cysteine
• Supporting glutathione synthesis
• Influencing cellular redox balance
• Assisting certain liver-processing
reactions

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
THE BRAIN CONNECTION
Glutathione and glutamate regulation
are both important to brain function.
Researchers have therefore
investigated NAC as an adjunct in areas
such as:
• Compulsive behaviors
• Substance-use disorders
• Mood disorders
• Neuroinflammation

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
WHAT ABOUT DAILY SUPPLEMENTATION?
General Antioxidant/Liver support: 600-
1,200 mg
Respiratory/Mucus clearing: 600-1,800 mg
Psychiatric/Neurological support. 1,200 -
2,400 mg

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
TEST BEFORE YOU GUESS
Low glutathione activity can reflect many
influences:
• Illness or chronic inflammation
• Poor protein intake
• Increased oxidative exposure
• Aging
• Medication use
• Metabolic dysfunction
• Genetic variation
NAC may provide support but it does not
explain why the burden exists.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
MEET PROFESSOR TIM SPECTOR
Tim Spector is a physician, epidemiologist
and professor at King's College London.
He founded the British Gut Project
and helped lead some of the world's largest
research into nutrition and the gut
microbiome.
He is also co-founder of ZOE, a nutrition-
science company studying how individuals
respond differently to food.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
His work helped popularize an important
idea:
There may be no single "perfect diet" for
everyone.
Our microbes are part of the equation.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
THE MICROBIAL WORLD WITHIN US
Your digestive tract contains
trillions of microorganisms.
This community, the gut microbiome,
interacts with:
Digestion
Immune function
Metabolism
Inflammation
The nervous system

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
Spector's work has helped bring this hidden
ecosystem into the mainstream
conversation about health.
We aren't simply feeding ourselves.
We're feeding an ecosystem. Here are his 8
rules to keep it healthy:

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
LESSON #1
DIVERSITY FEEDS DIVERSITY
One message associated with Spector's
work:
Eat a greater variety of plants.
Vegetables
Fruit
Beans
Whole grains
Nuts + seeds
Herbs + spices
The widely discussed goal?
30 different plants per week.
It isn't a magic number, it's a practical way
to encourage dietary diversity.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
LESSON #2
REDISCOVER FERMENTED FOOD
Yogurt. Kefir. Kimchi.
Sauerkraut. Miso. Tempeh.
Long before we understood the microbiome,
humans were transforming food with microbes.
Modern research suggests fermented foods
can influence the gut microbiome
and immune activity.
Spector regularly encourages incorporating
fermented foods into the diet. Ancient food
wisdom meets microbiome science.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
LESSON #3
FEED YOUR MICROBES
Probiotics get enormous attention.
But the microbes already living inside you
need something too:
FOOD.
Fiber and other compounds from plants
reach the colon, where microbes transform
them into biologically active metabolites.
Beans • onions • garlic • oats
lentils • seeds • vegetables • resistant starch
Don't just think about adding microbes.
Think about feeding them.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
LESSON #4
EAT MORE COLOR
Berries.Herbs. Spices.Coffee.Tea.
Extra-virgin olive oil.Dark cocoa.
Colorful vegetables.
Many contain polyphenols—plant
compounds that interact with our gut
microbes.
Spector has become a major advocate
for increasing polyphenol-rich foods.
Perhaps eating the rainbow isn't merely
about vitamins.
It's also about feeding microbial chemistry.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
LESSON #5
ULTRA-PROCESSED FOOD CHANGES THE
EQUATION
Spector has been outspoken about
our growing dependence on ultra-processed
foods.
The issue isn't simply calories.
Highly processed diets may contain fewer
intact plant structures and less fiber while
introducing combinations of additives rarely
found in traditional diets.
Rather than obsessing over every ingredient:
Build most meals around recognizable,
minimally processed foods.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
LESSON #6
GIVE YOUR GUT SOME QUIET TIME
Spector has also discussed the potential
benefits of allowing a longer overnight
period without food.
Between meals, the digestive system isn't
idle.
Patterns of intestinal movement help move
residual material through the digestive tract.
Instead of grazing from morning until
bedtime:
Consider giving digestion a nightly pause.
Sometimes wellness isn't about adding
another thing.
It's about stopping for a while.

Holisticentra
@holisticentral
LESSON #7
YOUR MOUTH MATTERS TOO
The microbiome doesn't suddenly begin
when food reaches the intestines.
The mouth has its own microbial ecosystem.
Oral and gut health are connected through
a continuous digestive pathway, and
researchers are now linking dementia to
poor mouth hygeine.
Brush, floss.
Clean between the teeth.
Care for the gums.

Holisticentra
@holisticentral
LESSON #8
YOUR GUT AND BRAIN ARE TALKING
One of the most fascinating areas
of microbiome research is the:
GUT-BRAIN AXIS
The gut and brain communicate through
the nervous system, immune pathways,
hormones and microbial metabolites.
This doesn't mean depression or anxiety
is simply "caused by the gut."
It means something more interesting:
The brain and digestive system
are part of an ongoing biological
conversation.

Holisticentra
@holisticentral
SPECTOR'S BIGGER MESSAGE
Perhaps Spector's most important
contribution isn't one food recommendation.
It's a different way of thinking about
nutrition.
Instead of asking:
"What is the perfect diet?"
Ask:
How diverse is my food?
How many plants am I eating?
Am I feeding my microbes?
How processed is my diet?
How does my body respond?
Nutrition may be far more personal
than we once believed.

WHAT A 2025 META-ANALYSIS REVEALED ABOUT
PARASITES & COLON CANCER...
A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF 70 STUDIES ASKS AN
IMPORTANT QUESTION: DO INTESTINAL
PARASITES PLAY A ROLE IN COLORECTAL
CANCER?

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
Why This Matters
Colorectal cancer is one of the leading
causes of cancer-related death
worldwide.
Scientists have spent decades studying
genetics, diet, inflammation, the
microbiome...
But another question has quietly
emerged:
Could certain intestinal parasites also be
involved?

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
The Study
Researchers analyzed:
V 70 published studies
V Data from 26 countries
V Thousands of patients
Using a systematic review and meta-
analysis, they combined the best available
evidence to look for patterns.
This is considered one of the highest levels
of evidence for identifying associations.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
What They Found
Across the studies...
Approximately 1 in 5 colorectal cancer patients
(19.7%) had evidence of an intestinal parasitic
infection.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
Which Parasites Appeared Most Often?
Among those most frequently reported
were:
• Schistosoma species
• Blastocystis species
• Cryptosporidium species
Not every parasite showed the same
relationship.
Some showed stronger associations than
others.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
Why Might This Happen?
Researchers have proposed several
possibilities.
Some parasites may:
• Create chronic inflammation
• Alter the gut microbiome
• Influence immune signaling
• Damage intestinal tissue over time

Holisticentral V
@holisticentral
A Bigger Question
Modern medicine increasingly recognizes
that chronic disease is rarely explained by
a single cause.
Instead, health often reflects an interaction
between:
• Diet
• The microbiome
• Environmental exposures
• Genetics
• Immune function
• Chronic infections
Parasites may be one piece of a much
larger biological puzzle.

Holisticentralv
@holisticentral
What Should We Do With This Information?
This study isn't an invitation to fear parasites.
It's an invitation to ask better questions.
Perhaps the future of medicine isn't simply
treating disease...
Perhaps it's understanding every factor that
quietly shapes health long before disease
appears.

Holisticentral V

What Is Berberine?
Berberine is a bright yellow plant compound
found in herbs such as:
• Barberry
• Oregon grape
• Goldenseal
• Chinese goldthread (Coptis)
For centuries it has been used in traditional
medicine.
Today, it is one of the most extensively
researched botanical compounds for
metabolic health.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
The Strongest Evidence
The best clinical evidence supports
berberine's role in helping improve:
V
Blood sugar regulation
V
Insulin sensitivity
V
LDL cholesterol
V
Triglycerides
V
Markers of metabolic syndrome
Researchers continue studying how these
effects occur.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
Meet AMPK
Your Cell's "Energy Sensor"
One of berberine's best-known actions is
activating AMP-activated protein kinase
(AMPK).
AMPK helps cells respond when energy is
low by encouraging:
• Better glucose utilization
• Fat oxidation
• Healthier metabolic signaling
Think of it as helping cells become more
metabolically efficient.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
Beyond Blood Sugar
Research suggests berberine may also
help support:
* Cardiovascular health
® Metabolic flexibility
60 Liver fat metabolism
SId Healthy lipid balance
These benefits appear to result from
multiple biological pathways, not a single
mechanism.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
The Gut Connection
One of the newest areas of research
involves the gut microbiome.
Scientists believe berberine may:
• Influence beneficial bacteria
• Alter microbial metabolites
• Affect inflammation-related signaling
The gut may be one reason berberine has
such wide-ranging metabolic effects.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
A Better Question
Instead of asking:
"Should everyone take berberine?"
Ask:
"What is my metabolism trying to tell me?"
Testing blood sugar, fasting insulin, HbA1c,
lipids, and liver health can help guide more
personalized decisions.

INTERMITTENT FASTING....
ANCIENT WISDOM. MODERN SCIENCE.
WHY GIVING YOUR BODY A BREAK FROM
EATING MAY CHANGE MORE THAN YOUR
WAISTLINE...

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
For most of human history....
People didn't eat every few hours.
Our ancestors naturally experienced periods
without food due to hunting, gathering,
seasonal changes, and religious traditions.
Today, researchers are rediscovering what the
body does during those natural fasting periods.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
What Happens When You Fast?
After your body uses the energy from your last
meal, it begins to shift toward stored fuel.
During this transition, researchers have observed
changes in:
• Insulin levels
• Fat metabolism
• Cellular repair pathways
• Inflammatory signaling
• Hormonal balance
The exact timing varies from person to person.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
Research Suggests Intermittent Fasting May
Support:
V Metabolic flexibility
V Improved insulin sensitivity
V Healthy weight management
V Cardiovascular health
V Reduced oxidative stress
V Healthy inflammatory balance
V Brain health and cognitive function

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
Meet Autophagy
In 2016, Japanese scientist Yoshinori Ohsumi
received the Nobel Prize for discoveries that
helped explain autophagy.
Autophagy is the body's natural cellular
recycling process that helps remove damaged
cellular components.
Scientists continue studying
how fasting, exercise, and nutrient availability
influence this process.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
Intermittent Fasting Isn't Starvation
Starvation is an uncontrolled lack of food.
Intermittent fasting is a planned eating
schedule where adequate nutrition is still
consumed during eating periods.
Quality nutrition still matters.
What you eat remains just as important as
when you eat.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
A Beginner's Schedule
Start simple.
12:12
Fast for 12 hours.
Eat during a 12-hour window.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
Many people gradually progress to:
14:10
Or
16:8
Example:
Finish dinner at 7 PM.
Have your first meal at 11 AM.
This approach has been the most widely
studied in human intermittent fasting research.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
During the Fast
Generally choose beverages with little or no
calories, such as:
Water
• Black coffee (if tolerated)
* Unsweetened tea
Some people also use mineral water or
electrolytes without added sugar, depending on
their needs.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
Breaking the Fast
Avoid the temptation to binge.
Instead choose:
Protein
Healthy fats
Fiber-rich vegetables
Whole foods
A nutrient-dense meal supports steady energy
and satiety better than highly processed foods.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
Who Should NOT Fast Without Medical
Guidance?
Intermittent fasting may not be appropriate for
everyone.
Speak with your healthcare professional if you
are:
• Pregnant or breastfeeding
• Underweight
• Living with an eating disorder or history of one
• Taking medications that affect blood sugar
• Managing diabetes or other significant
medical conditions
Individual needs vary.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
The Bigger Lesson
Your body wasn't designed to be digesting food
every waking hour.
It was designed to alternate between periods of
nourishment and periods of repair.
Perhaps wellness isn't always about adding
more...
Sometimes it's about creating space for the body
to do what it already knows how to do.

FAT, AND WATER...
IT ALSO DEPENDS ON DOZENS OF MINERALS
TO PERFORM MILLIONS OF CHEMICAL
REACTIONS EVERY SECOND.
WITHOUT THEM, LIFE SIMPLY DOESN'T
WORK...

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
Minerals Make Life Possible
Minerals help your body:
• Produce energy (ATP)
• Conduct nerve signals
• Contract muscles
• Build bones and teeth
• Balance fluids
• Regulate hormones
• Support immunity
• Repair DNA
Every cell depends on them.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
Every Organ Needs Minerals
Heart → magnesium, potassium, calcium
Brain → iodine, iron, zinc, magnesium
Bones → calcium, magnesium, phosphorus,
boron
ge Thyroid → iodine, selenium
Blood → iron, copper
• Immune system → zinc, selenium
The body works as a team.

Holisticentraly
@holisticentral
Modern Life Can Challenge Mineral Status
Researchers continue studying how mineral
intake may be influenced by factors such as:
• diets low in nutrient-dense foods
• some highly processed foods
• certain medications
• gastrointestinal disorders affecting absorption
• chronic diarrhea or vomiting
• increased sweating
• some life stages such as pregnancy or older
adulthood
Not everyone is deficient, but mineral intake is
an important part of overall nutrition.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
Enter Humic & Fulvic
Long before scientists studied them...
Nature had already created them.
They form as plants, microorganisms, and
organic matter slowly decompose in healthy
soils over many years.
They are among nature's most complex
organic compounds.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
What is Fulvic Acid?
Fulvic acid is
• very small
• water soluble
• rich in oxygen-containing functional groups
• naturally present in healthy soil
Researchers are studying how it interacts with
minerals and other compounds in laboratory
and animal models, and how these interactions
might influence nutrient availability.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
What is Humic Acid?
Humic acid is
• much larger
• more complex
• less water soluble
• abundant in rich fertile soils
Scientists are investigating its antioxidant
properties, interactions with the gut
environment, and effects on microbial
communities.

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
Why Researchers Are Interested
Current research is exploring whether humic and
fulvic substances may:
V support mineral transport
V influence the gut microbiome
V contribute antioxidant activity
V interact with immune signaling
V bind certain metals and other compounds in
laboratory settings

Holisticentral
@holisticentral
Healthy Soil → Healthy Plants → Healthy
People?
Modern agriculture has dramatically increased
food production, utilizing pesticides that have
degraded the soil over time.
Scientists now continue to study how soil health
including organic matter and microbial
diversityinfluences nutrient cycling, crop quality,
and ecosystem resilience.
Healthy soil supports healthy ecosystems.

@holisticentral
Taking fulvic and humic minerals daily can

enhance the body and brain with vital missing
